_doc: GENERATED by tools/read_st_cyr_register.py --build. The death page is PROSE — eleven sentences with no delimiter — so its structure is hand-read in the DEATHS table of the tool and the gate proves every entry_as_printed is still byte-for-byte the line it was read from. One row is one named person: an entry naming a child and its father carries two readings. Hand-edit and --check says so.

list.title: Father St. Cyr's Chicago death and burial page, 1834-1837, as printed in the Illinois Catholic Historical Review vol. 4

the_ladder: Four of the eleven entries fall in 1835 and are scene-year deaths at Chicago on named days. A death is not a residence and none is asserted; the one identity this page settles, Thomas Owen, is settled in crosswalk.json and changes no resident record.

cells.entry_as_printed: On the 17th of July 1835, I performed the ceremonies of the ecclesiastical burial on the corpse of Julian Andrews, 18 days old. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 6 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1835-07-17. SCENE YEAR. 18 days old, so born about 29 June 1835 by the same arithmetic. No parent is named, which is unusual for an infant burial and is the page's silence, not an omission here.

cells.entry_as_printed: Died at Chicago the 15th of October, 1835, Thomas Owen, agent of the Indians. On the 17th performed the ceremonies of the church on the corpse. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 7 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1835-10-15. SCENE YEAR, and the one entry on either page that reaches an attested resident. Died at Chicago 15 October 1835; buried on the 17th.

cells.entry_as_printed: Died at Chicago, Ill., the 16th of July 1836, John . . . After the reception of the last sacraments, on the 17th, I performed the ceremonies of the church on the corpse in the presence of a large crowd of Germans (he had been stabbed). J. M. I. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 8 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1836-07-16. The surname is LOST on the page — printed as an ellipsis — and none is invented. Stabbed; buried on the 17th before a large crowd of Germans.

cells.entry_as_printed: On the 11th of February 1837, I, the undersigned, performed the ceremonies of thee rites of the Catholic Church on the corpse of Ann Donovan, who died the 14th inst., 9 years old. - J. M. I. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 9 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1837-02-14. Beyond the window the ticket named. The page's own dates are inconsistent: the burial is written 11 February and the death "the 14th inst.", which puts the burial before the death. Both are carried as printed. Outside the June 1834 - July 1836 window T-0573 named. Read anyway: the page carries eleven entries, the ticket counted the eight inside its window, and leaving three unread to match a number would be the wrong repair.

cells.entry_as_printed: Chicago, Ill. On the 24th of February 1837, I, the undersigned, performed the ceremonies of the rites of the Catholic Church on the corpse of Celestain Vilmain, 5 months old. - J. M. I. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 10 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1837-02-24. Beyond the window the ticket named. Five months old. Outside the June 1834 - July 1836 window T-0573 named. Read anyway: the page carries eleven entries, the ticket counted the eight inside its window, and leaving three unread to match a number would be the wrong repair.

cells.entry_as_printed: Chicago, March 2, 1837. I, the undersigned, performed the ceremonies of the Church on the corpse of Jerome Beaubien, who died on the 1st of March. Aged 2 years. - J. M. I. - St. Cyr

records.notes: Decedent of death entry 11 of 11 on Father St. Cyr's death page, 1837-03-01. Beyond the window the ticket named. Died 1 March 1837, aged 2; buried on the 2nd. A Beaubien child, and the Beaubiens are a family this reconstruction already holds — the identity is NOT joined here. Outside the June 1834 - July 1836 window T-0573 named. Read anyway: the page carries eleven entries, the ticket counted the eight inside its window, and leaving three unread to match a number would be the wrong repair.

the_count_the_ticket_carried: T-0573 said "nine deaths and burials, June 1834 to July 1836". The page carries ELEVEN entries: eight inside that window and three of February and March 1837 outside it. All eleven are read. Nine is not a count this page supports at any boundary, and the discrepancy is reported rather than made to fit.
